When these social apps launched.Friendster: Founder Jonathan Abrams' site hit millions of users fast, but slow servers and clutter let MySpace and Facebook overtake it.
When these social apps launched.LinkedIn: Founded by Reid Hoffman, it was bought by Microsoft in 2016 for about 26 billion dollars, one of the largest tech buyouts then.
When these social apps launched.Facebook: It began in a Harvard dorm as 'TheFacebook', limited to college students, and dropped 'The' from its name in 2005.
When these social apps launched.YouTube: The first video, 'Me at the zoo', was posted by cofounder Jawed Karim on 23 April 2005. Google bought the site in 2006.
When these social apps launched.Twitter: Its original 140-character limit came from the 160-character SMS cap, leaving room for the username. It was renamed X in 2023.
When these social apps launched.Tumblr: David Karp's blogging platform sold to Yahoo for about 1.1 billion dollars, and later changed hands for far less.
When these social apps launched.WhatsApp: Founded by two ex-Yahoo employees, it was bought by Facebook in 2014 for about 19 billion dollars while still ad-free.
When these social apps launched.Instagram: It began as a check-in app called Burbn, and Facebook bought it in 2012 for 1 billion dollars when it had only 13 employees.
When these social apps launched.Snapchat: It began as Picaboo, and its vanishing messages were the hook, an idea later copied by Instagram and Facebook.
When these social apps launched.Threads: Meta's text app signed up 100 million people in about five days after launch in July 2023, a record at the time.

One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Gladiator: Russell Crowe's Maximus won Best Picture, and Oliver Reed died during filming, so his last scenes were completed digitally.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Shrek: It won the first Best Animated Feature Oscar. Chris Farley had recorded Shrek's lines before he died, and Mike Myers took over.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Ice Age: Scrat, the acorn-chasing squirrel-rat, started as a minor gag and became the series' mascot.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Lost in Translation: Sofia Coppola's Tokyo story won the Oscar for screenplay, and what Bill Murray whispers at the end is never revealed.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Mean Girls: Tina Fey wrote it, adapting the non-fiction book Queen Bees and Wannabes.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Batman Begins: Christopher Nolan's reboot introduced the Tumbler, a military-style Batmobile, and a darker tone.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Casino Royale: It was Daniel Craig's first outing as 007, adapting Ian Fleming's first Bond novel from 1953.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Superbad: Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg started writing it as teens, around age 13.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.The Dark Knight: Heath Ledger won a posthumous Oscar as the Joker, and parts were filmed with IMAX cameras.
One 2000s hit per year: put them in orde.Avatar: James Cameron's film became the highest-grossing movie ever, at roughly 2.9 billion dollars, using new 3D cameras.

Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Haiyuan, China: It killed about 200,000 people in Gansu, and landslides buried entire villages.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Quetta, Pakistan: It destroyed the city in 1935, killing tens of thousands, and a major British military base was hit hard.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Ashgabat, Turkmenistan: It destroyed the Turkmen capital, and Soviet authorities censored news of the disaster for years.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Tabas, Iran: It struck Iran's Tabas region, killing around 15,000 or more, mostly in mud-brick homes.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Spitak, Armenia: It killed about 25,000 in Armenia, and the Soviet Union accepted foreign aid, which was unusual at the time.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.İzmit, Turkey: It hit northwestern Turkey along the North Anatolian Fault, killing over 17,000.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Gujarat, India: It struck Bhuj on Republic Day, killing around 20,000.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Bam, Iran: The ancient mud-brick Arg-e Bam citadel was largely destroyed, and about 26,000 people died.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Kashmir: A magnitude 7.6 quake killed over 80,000 people, mostly in Pakistan, and devastated Muzaffarabad.
Earthquakes across Asia, in order.Gorkha, Nepal: It killed nearly 9,000 in Nepal and collapsed Kathmandu's historic Dharahara tower.

Spaces on the board in these games.Tic-tac-toe: With perfect play it always ends in a draw, and there are 255,168 possible games.
Spaces on the board in these games.Backgammon: Related dice-and-race games date back around 5,000 years in Mesopotamia, making it among the oldest board games.
Spaces on the board in these games.Monopoly: Based on The Landlord's Game, created by Lizzie Magie to show the evils of land monopoly.
Spaces on the board in these games.Connect Four: A 1988 analysis proved the first player wins with perfect play.
Spaces on the board in these games.Chess: Estimates of its possible games exceed the number of atoms in the observable universe.
Spaces on the board in these games.Shogi: Captured pieces can be reused by the capturer, a rule that sets it apart from chess.
Spaces on the board in these games.Xiangqi (Chinese chess): Pieces sit on intersections, a river divides the board and generals are confined to a palace.
Spaces on the board in these games.Chinese checkers: It is not Chinese: it was invented in Germany in 1892 as Stern-Halma.
Spaces on the board in these games.Scrabble: Invented by architect Alfred Butts in the 1930s, it was originally called Criss-Crosswords.
Spaces on the board in these games.Go: This ancient Chinese game has more possible positions than atoms in the universe, and AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016.

NBA legends, by rookie season.Bill Russell: He won 11 championships in 13 seasons with the Celtics and later became the NBA's first Black head coach.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Wilt Chamberlain: He scored 100 points in a game on 2 March 1962, a record that still stands.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Kareem Abdul-Jabbar: His skyhook made him the league's all-time leading scorer for nearly 39 years, until LeBron James passed him in 2023.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Larry Bird: He won three MVPs in a row from 1984 to 1986, and his rivalry with Magic Johnson revived the league.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Michael Jordan: He won six titles and six Finals MVPs, and his Bulls never lost an NBA Finals series.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Shaquille O'Neal: He shattered backboards early in his career, which led the NBA to change its rim design.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Kobe Bryant: He entered the league straight out of high school and spent all 20 seasons with the Lakers.
NBA legends, by rookie season.LeBron James: He too came straight from high school, and since 2023 he has been the NBA's all-time leading scorer.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Stephen Curry: He revolutionised the game with three-pointers, setting the single-season record of 402 in 2015-16.
NBA legends, by rookie season.Giannis Antetokounmpo: Born in Athens to Nigerian parents, the Greek Freak won MVP in 2019 and 2020.

Ballets, by premiere year.La Sylphide: La Sylphide is among the oldest surviving Romantic ballets, and it made dancing on pointe a signature of the ethereal style.
Ballets, by premiere year.Giselle: Giselle features ghostly spirits called Wilis, and it remains a showcase for ballerinas.
Ballets, by premiere year.Coppélia: Coppélia is a comic ballet about a doll that seems alive, and it is famous for its cheerful music by Léo Delibes.
Ballets, by premiere year.Swan Lake: Swan Lake flopped at its Moscow premiere, and it only became a hit after Petipa and Ivanov restaged it after the composer's death.
Ballets, by premiere year.The Sleeping Beauty: The Sleeping Beauty was Tchaikovsky's second ballet, and he reportedly considered it among his best scores.
Ballets, by premiere year.The Nutcracker: The Nutcracker was not a hit at first, but it is now performed worldwide every Christmas, and funds many companies.
Ballets, by premiere year.The Firebird: The Firebird made Stravinsky famous overnight, and it was his first collaboration with Sergei Diaghilev's Ballets Russes.
Ballets, by premiere year.The Rite of Spring: The Rite of Spring caused a near riot at its Paris premiere, and its rhythms changed the course of modern music.
Ballets, by premiere year.Appalachian Spring: Appalachian Spring features Aaron Copland's score and Martha Graham's choreography, and it won him a Pulitzer Prize for music.
Ballets, by premiere year.Spartacus: Spartacus is Khachaturian's ballet, and its Adagio became widely known as the theme to the British TV series The Onedin Line.

When these came to the end of the line.Pony Express shuts down: It lasted only about 18 months before the transcontinental telegraph made it obsolete in October 1861.
When these came to the end of the line.Model T production ends: About 15 million Model Ts were built between 1908 and 1927.
When these came to the end of the line.UK mainline steam ends: British Rail's last scheduled steam services ran in August 1968, though heritage lines keep steam alive.
When these came to the end of the line.DeLorean production ends: Its stainless steel body and gull-wing doors earned fame in Back to the Future, but the company collapsed in 1982.
When these came to the end of the line.Citroën 2CV production ends: It was designed so a farmer could carry eggs across a field without breaking them.
When these came to the end of the line.Classic Mini production ends: Built from 1959, it ended in 2000 after more than five million had been made.
When these came to the end of the line.Concorde retired: The last commercial flights were in October 2003, and only 20 were built, 14 for airline service.
When these came to the end of the line.Routemaster service ends: London's red double-decker left regular service in 2005, though heritage routes continue.
When these came to the end of the line.Space Shuttle retired: Atlantis landed in July 2011 on the final mission, and six orbiters were built, five of which flew in space.
When these came to the end of the line.Boeing 747 production ends: Boeing delivered the last jumbo in January 2023, and its hump gave the plane its iconic shape.

How fast these move.Escalator: Escalators move at about half a metre a second, and Hong Kong's Central-Mid-Levels escalator is the longest outdoor covered system.
How fast these move.Walking: Olympic race walkers keep over 14 km/h for 20 km, almost three times a stroll's pace, without ever letting both feet leave the ground.
How fast these move.Jogging: Marathon winners run at about double this pace for over two hours.
How fast these move.Commuter cycling: The bicycle is the most energy-efficient human-powered transport per kilometre.
How fast these move.City traffic: Many cities set this limit, and pedestrians hit at 30 km/h are far more likely to survive than at 50.
How fast these move.Highway driving: Limits in many countries run about 100 to 130 km/h, and some stretches of Germany's Autobahn have no limit.
How fast these move.High-speed train: Japan's Shinkansen opened in 1964, and its average delays are measured in seconds.
How fast these move.Airliner at cruise: Airliners cruise at about Mach 0.85, high up where the thin air creates less drag.
How fast these move.Speed of sound: Sound travels at about 343 metres per second in air at 20 degrees, much faster through water and steel.
How fast these move.Concorde: Concorde flew faster than twice the speed of sound, so its flights from London arrived in New York earlier by the clock than they left.

Venerable contests, by first edition.Epsom Derby: The race's name was reportedly settled by a coin toss between the Earl of Derby and Sir Charles Bunbury, and Derby won, lending his title to a global word.
Venerable contests, by first edition.The Boat Race: Oxford and Cambridge row about 6.8 km up the Thames, and the very first Boat Race in 1829 was held at Henley.
Venerable contests, by first edition.Henley Royal Regatta: This regatta has been held on the Thames since 1839 and still keeps traditions such as a strict dress code in its Stewards' Enclosure.
Venerable contests, by first edition.America's Cup: It began as a race around the Isle of Wight won by the yacht America, whose name gave the trophy its name, and the US held it for 132 years.
Venerable contests, by first edition.The Open (golf): The very first Open had only eight players, at Prestwick in Scotland, and winner Willie Park Sr. took home the Challenge Belt.
Venerable contests, by first edition.FA Cup: The oldest national football knockout competition lets clubs of every level enter, so tiny non-league sides can end up facing giants.
Venerable contests, by first edition.US tennis championships: Held first at Newport, Rhode Island, this championship grew into the US Open, which is now played at Flushing Meadows in New York.
Venerable contests, by first edition.French tennis championships: Better known as Roland Garros, this clay-court Grand Slam was initially restricted to French club members until 1925.
Venerable contests, by first edition.Australasian tennis champs: Today it is the Australian Open. It began at Warehouse Cricket Ground in Melbourne, and has been held in many cities over its history.
Venerable contests, by first edition.PGA Championship: This golf major was founded after a lunch in New York, and Jim Barnes won the first edition; it is now played in May.

Landmark telescopes through history.Lippershey's patent request: Hans Lippershey, a Dutch spectacle maker, applied for a patent on a device for seeing faraway things, though officials declined to grant it.
Landmark telescopes through history.Galileo's first telescope: Galileo heard of the Dutch invention, built his own, and soon discovered Jupiter's four big moons, the phases of Venus, and mountains on the Moon.
Landmark telescopes through history.Newton's reflector: Isaac Newton's reflecting telescope used a curved mirror instead of a lens, which avoids the colored fringes that plagued early refractors.
Landmark telescopes through history.Herschel's 40-foot telescope: William Herschel's giant reflector, with a tube about 12 meters long, helped him spot two moons of Saturn, though it was awkward to use.
Landmark telescopes through history.Leviathan of Parsonstown: The Leviathan, built by the Earl of Rosse in Ireland, was the world's largest telescope for about 70 years and revealed the spiral shape of galaxies like M51.
Landmark telescopes through history.Yerkes 40-inch refractor: The Yerkes lens still holds the record as the largest refracting telescope ever used for research, because bigger lenses sag under their own weight.
Landmark telescopes through history.Hooker 100-inch telescope: At Mount Wilson, the Hooker mirror let Edwin Hubble show that Andromeda is a separate galaxy and that the universe is expanding.
Landmark telescopes through history.Hale 200-inch telescope: The Hale telescope on Palomar Mountain was the world's largest for nearly three decades, and its 200-inch mirror took years to cool and grind.
Landmark telescopes through history.Keck I: Keck I on Mauna Kea pioneered a mirror made of 36 hexagonal segments, adjusted continuously to act as a single huge surface.
Landmark telescopes through history.Very Large Telescope (UT1): The VLT's first unit saw first light in Chile's Atacama Desert; later, four 8.2-meter telescopes could combine to act as one enormous instrument.

Iconic space images, in order.First photo of Earth (V-2): A camera on a captured German V-2 rocket, launched from New Mexico, took it from about 105 km up.
Iconic space images, in order.Earthrise: Astronaut Bill Anders snapped it while orbiting the Moon on Apollo 8, famously showing Earth rising over the lunar horizon.
Iconic space images, in order.The Blue Marble: The Apollo 17 crew shot it on their way to the Moon, and it is one of the most reproduced photographs ever taken.
Iconic space images, in order.First photo on Venus' surface: Soviet lander Venera 9 sent it, then survived about 53 minutes in crushing pressure and furnace heat.
Iconic space images, in order.First photo on Mars' surface: The Viking 1 lander sent the first one in 1976, showing a rocky, rust-colored plain.
Iconic space images, in order.Pale Blue Dot: Voyager 1 turned its camera back from about 6 billion km away at Carl Sagan's request, and Earth appears as a speck.
Iconic space images, in order.Hubble Deep Field: Hubble stared at an apparently empty patch of sky for ten days and revealed about 3,000 galaxies.
Iconic space images, in order.First image of an exoplanet: It showed 2M1207b, a planet orbiting a brown dwarf, captured by the Very Large Telescope in Chile.
Iconic space images, in order.First image of a black hole: The Event Horizon Telescope linked radio dishes across the globe into one planet-sized instrument to image the black hole in galaxy M87.
Iconic space images, in order.Webb's First Deep Field: It looked at the galaxy cluster SMACS 0723, a patch of sky about the size of a grain of sand held at arm's length.

Animal facts measured in metres.A giraffe's tongue: A giraffe's tongue is dark purple-black, which is thought to protect it from sunburn while feeding.
Animal facts measured in metres.An elephant's trunk: An elephant's trunk can hold about eight litres of water, which the animal sprays into its mouth rather than drinking through it.
Animal facts measured in metres.Height of a giraffe: A giraffe has the same seven neck vertebrae as a human, only enormously elongated.
Animal facts measured in metres.Red kangaroo's single leap: A red kangaroo can cover up to 8 metres in a single bound and travels at about 60 km/h.
Animal facts measured in metres.Length of a whale shark: The largest fish alive, it filters plankton, and each one has a unique pattern of spots.
Animal facts measured in metres.Length of a blue whale: The largest animal known to have lived, its calls are among the loudest of any animal, over 180 decibels.
Animal facts measured in metres.Lion's mane jelly tentacles: A tentacle of the lion's mane jelly can be longer than a blue whale, yet it is a thin, stinging thread.
Animal facts measured in metres.Sperm whale dive depth: A sperm whale dives over two kilometres to hunt giant squid, and often bears scars from their suckers.
Animal facts measured in metres.Howler monkey call carries: A howler monkey's hyoid bone amplifies its roar, making it among the loudest land animals.
Animal facts measured in metres.Rüppell's vulture altitude: One of these vultures was hit by an aeroplane at about 11,300 m over Ivory Coast in 1973, a record height for a bird.

Birth years of these jazz greats.Scott Joplin: The King of Ragtime wrote the Maple Leaf Rag. He received a posthumous Pulitzer Prize special citation in 1976.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Duke Ellington: He composed over a thousand pieces and led his orchestra for about fifty years, starting at Harlem's Cotton Club.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Louis Armstrong: Nicknamed Satchmo, he made the trumpet a solo instrument and popularized scat singing, then topped charts with What a Wonderful World.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Count Basie: The Kansas City bandleader was known for sparse piano playing: sometimes just a few notes were enough to make his band swing.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Billie Holiday: Lady Day recorded Strange Fruit, a haunting 1939 protest against lynching, and it became one of the most famous songs of the era.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Charlie Parker: Bird co-founded bebop with Dizzy Gillespie in the 1940s, and died at only 34.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Miles Davis: His 1959 album Kind of Blue is widely cited as the best-selling jazz album ever.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Nina Simone: A classically trained pianist who wanted to be a concert pianist, she was rejected by the Curtis Institute and became a civil rights voice.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Herbie Hancock: He played with Miles Davis in his twenties; his 1983 hit Rockit featured turntable scratching.
Birth years of these jazz greats.Wynton Marsalis: In 1983 he won Grammys in both jazz and classical categories, and in 1997 his Blood on the Fields won the first Pulitzer awarded to jazz.

Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Start of Spring: Lichun marks the beginning of spring in the Chinese calendar, falling midway between the winter solstice and the spring equinox.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Rain Water: Yushui marks the time when rainfall begins to replace snow.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Awakening of Insects: Jingzhe: thunder is said to wake hibernating insects, a signal for farmers to start plowing.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Clear and Bright: Qingming is also a tomb-sweeping festival, when families honor ancestors by cleaning graves and bringing offerings.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Grain Buds: Xiaoman: wheat and other grains are filling out but are not yet ripe.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Start of Autumn: Liqiu is the name of a season starting in the heat of August, so it often feels like deep summer.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.White Dew: Nights are cool enough that dew forms on the grass, white in the morning light.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Frost's Descent: Shuangjiang marks the first frosts and is the last of autumn's six solar terms.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Major Snow: Daxue is the 21st of the 24 terms, when snow deepens across northern China.
Chinese solar terms, from the start of s.Major Cold: Dahan is the last of the 24 solar terms. After it spring begins again, and Chinese New Year often falls close by.

Netflix through the years.Netflix founded: Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph started it in California, years before home internet was fast enough to stream a film.
Netflix through the years.DVD rental site opens: Early Netflix mailed DVDs in red envelopes, charging per rental with late fees, before it ever tried a subscription.
Netflix through the years.Monthly subscription: Flat monthly pricing with no due dates and no late fees was the idea that set Netflix apart from video rental stores.
Netflix through the years.Netflix Prize contest: Netflix offered $1 million to anyone who could improve its movie recommendations by 10 percent; a team finally won in 2009.
Netflix through the years.Streaming begins: The first 'Watch Now' streaming gave US subscribers a small library playable on a computer, long before smart TVs.
Netflix through the years.Qwikster fiasco: Netflix announced it would split DVDs into a separate service called Qwikster, then dropped the idea within weeks after backlash.
Netflix through the years.House of Cards: Its first big original drama, a political thriller, dropped a whole season at once and helped popularize binge-watching.
Netflix through the years.Goes global: In January 2016 Netflix switched on service in about 130 new countries at once, announced by Reed Hastings at CES.
Netflix through the years.Ad-supported plan: After years of saying it never would, Netflix added a cheaper tier with commercials in late 2022.
Netflix through the years.Password-sharing crackdown: Netflix began charging extra for viewers outside an account's household, and the company then added millions of subscribers.

Units of digital information, by size.Bit: Short for 'binary digit', it holds a 0 or a 1, and the word was coined by statistician John Tukey.
Units of digital information, by size.Nibble: It is half a byte, enough for a single hexadecimal digit, and its name is a pun on 'byte'.
Units of digital information, by size.Byte: Werner Buchholz coined the term in 1956, spelling it with a y to avoid confusion with 'bit'.
Units of digital information, by size.Kilobyte: In SI it is 1,000 bytes, while older convention made it 1,024, hence the separate term 'kibibyte'.
Units of digital information, by size.Megabyte: A full-size novel in plain text is only about one megabyte, far less than a single phone photo.
Units of digital information, by size.Gigabyte: A single-layer DVD holds about 4.7 of them, and a typical streaming movie uses a few per hour.
Units of digital information, by size.Terabyte: A common size for a modern laptop or hard drive, it holds roughly a thousand gigabytes.
Units of digital information, by size.Petabyte: The Large Hadron Collider produces tens of petabytes of data a year, a flood far too large to keep it all.
Units of digital information, by size.Exabyte: Global internet traffic is measured in hundreds of exabytes per month, driven mostly by video.
Units of digital information, by size.Zettabyte: Estimates put all the data created worldwide each year at well over a hundred zettabytes.

Italian islands by area.Burano: Famed for its brightly painted houses and lace, it is said the colors helped fishermen spot home through the fog.
Italian islands by area.Murano: Venice moved its glassmakers here in 1291, partly to reduce fire risk and guard trade secrets.
Italian islands by area.Capri: Roman emperor Tiberius ruled from his villa here for his last decade, and the Blue Grotto glows an unreal blue.
Italian islands by area.Lampedusa: Closer to Tunisia than to Sicily, it is Italy's southernmost inhabited island, and its Rabbit Beach is often ranked among the world's best.
Italian islands by area.Ischia: This volcanic island in the Bay of Naples has hot springs, and Greeks founded one of their earliest Italian colonies here, Pithekoussai.
Italian islands by area.Pantelleria: A volcanic island nearer Tunisia than Sicily, it is known for dammusi stone houses and passito wine from vines grown in pits.
Italian islands by area.Sant'Antioco: Linked to Sardinia by a causeway, it hosts Sulky, founded by Phoenicians in the eighth century BC, among the oldest cities on Sardinia.
Italian islands by area.Elba: Napoleon was exiled here in 1814 and escaped in 1815 to launch his Hundred Days.
Italian islands by area.Sardinia: Thousands of Bronze Age stone towers called nuraghi dot the island, which is also known for its many centenarians.
Italian islands by area.Sicily: The Mediterranean's largest island is home to Mount Etna, Europe's most active volcano, and to remarkable Greek temples at Agrigento.

When these famous assassinations happene.Philip II of Macedon: He was killed by his bodyguard at his daughter's wedding; his son Alexander then took the throne.
When these famous assassinations happene.Julius Caesar: Roughly 60 senators conspired in the attack on the Ides of March.
When these famous assassinations happene.Caligula: Guards killed him, and his uncle Claudius, found hiding behind a curtain, was made emperor.
When these famous assassinations happene.Domitian: Court officials killed him, and the Senate condemned his memory, erasing his name from monuments.
When these famous assassinations happene.Commodus: His wrestling partner strangled him; the film Gladiator portrays his death very differently.
When these famous assassinations happene.Caracalla: A soldier attacked him by the roadside; the plot was organised by his guard prefect, Macrinus.
When these famous assassinations happene.Aurelian: He was reportedly killed by officers who feared punishment because of a forged list of names.
When these famous assassinations happene.Thomas Becket: Knights killed the archbishop in Canterbury Cathedral after King Henry II's angry words; he was made a saint soon after.
When these famous assassinations happene.Edward II of England: Deposed by his wife Isabella and Roger Mortimer, he died in Berkeley Castle; the red-hot poker story is a later legend.
When these famous assassinations happene.James I of Scotland: A band of nobles stabbed him at a Perth friary; he reportedly tried hiding in a sewer, which had been blocked.

When these brand mascots were born.Michelin Man: Also called Bibendum, he is made of stacked tyres. The name comes from a Latin phrase meaning 'now is the time to drink'.
When these brand mascots were born.Mr. Peanut: A schoolboy, Antonio Gentile, won a contest with his sketch, and a commercial artist then added the top hat, monocle and cane.
When these brand mascots were born.Jolly Green Giant: Early on he was a scowling figure in a bearskin, but became smiling and friendly with his famous 'ho, ho, ho'.
When these brand mascots were born.Elsie the Cow: Borden's mascot was given a husband named Elmer, and the glue brand Elmer's was named after him.
When these brand mascots were born.Tony the Tiger: For decades Thurl Ravenscroft voiced the 'They're gr-r-reat!' tiger, and also sang 'You're a Mean One, Mr. Grinch'.
When these brand mascots were born.Mr. Clean: The bald, muscled cleaner is known as Mr. Proper in much of Europe.
When these brand mascots were born.Ronald McDonald: Willard Scott, later the Today show's weatherman, played the first clown in 1963, in Washington, D.C.
When these brand mascots were born.Pillsbury Doughboy: Known as Poppin' Fresh, he giggles when poked in the belly, and an advertising man dreamed him up for biscuit dough.
When these brand mascots were born.Energizer Bunny: The drum-beating pink rabbit began as a parody of rival Duracell's own bunny ads, and kept on going and going.
When these brand mascots were born.GEICO Gecko: The character began as a pun, since many people say the company name as 'gecko'.

Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.Morris worm: Written by a Cornell student, it spread faster than intended, slowed much of the early internet, and led to a first US conviction for computer fraud.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.Pentium FDIV bug: A flaw in Intel's chip division table gave rare wrong answers. Replacing the chips eventually cost the company about $475 million.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.Ariane 5 explosion: The rocket blew up about 37 seconds after launch because reused Ariane 4 software choked on a number too big for its format.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.Melissa virus: It spread by emailing itself to the first 50 contacts in a victim's address book, jamming mail servers within days.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.ILOVEYOU worm: Arriving as an email with that subject line, it overwrote files and reached tens of millions of computers within days.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.Stuxnet discovered: Widely reported to be a US-Israeli creation, this worm targeted Iranian uranium centrifuges and physically damaged them.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.Heartbleed: A missing length check in OpenSSL let attackers read chunks of server memory. It is named for the 'heartbeat' feature it abused.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.WannaCry: This ransomware used a leaked NSA exploit, and its spread was largely halted when a researcher registered a kill-switch domain.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.Log4Shell: A flaw in the Java logging library Log4j let attackers run code on a server just by getting it to log a crafted line of text.
Famous bugs, worms and meltdowns.CrowdStrike global outage: A faulty security-software update crashed roughly 8.5 million Windows machines and grounded flights around the world.

When these dream cars debuted.Chevrolet Corvette: It was the first mass-produced American sports car, with a fiberglass body, and only 300 were built in its first year.
When these dream cars debuted.Mercedes 300SL Gullwing: Its doors hinge from the roof because of a tubular frame, and it was the first production car with fuel injection.
When these dream cars debuted.Shelby Cobra: Carroll Shelby shoehorned an American Ford V8 into a lightweight British AC Ace to create this snake.
When these dream cars debuted.Lamborghini Miura: It pioneered the mid-engine V12 layout for road cars, and it was named for a famed breed of Spanish fighting bulls.
When these dream cars debuted.Ferrari Testarossa: Its name means red head in Italian, for the red cam covers on its engine, and it became a star of Miami Vice.
When these dream cars debuted.Ferrari F40: It was the last Ferrari approved by Enzo Ferrari himself, and the first road car to reach 200 mph.
When these dream cars debuted.McLaren F1: Gordon Murray's design put the driver in the centre seat with passengers either side, and it held the production-car speed record for years.
When these dream cars debuted.Bugatti Veyron: With 1,001 horsepower and a 16-cylinder engine, it was the first production car to top 400 km/h.
When these dream cars debuted.LaFerrari: The name simply means The Ferrari in Italian, and its hybrid system combines a V12 with electric motors.
When these dream cars debuted.Bugatti Chiron: It is named after Louis Chiron, a Monegasque racing driver who won for Bugatti in the 1920s and 30s.

Characters' ages in their famous stories.Alice (in Wonderland): In Through the Looking-Glass, she says she is seven and a half, though Lewis Carroll's model Alice Liddell was a bit older.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Harry Potter, book one: Hagrid delivers his Hogwarts letter on his eleventh birthday, and he shares a 31 July birthday with J.K. Rowling.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Juliet Capulet: Lady Capulet says she is not yet fourteen; Shakespeare made her younger than in his source poem, where she was sixteen.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Katniss Everdeen (book 1): Katniss volunteers in her little sister's place, and the Reaping draws names from children aged twelve to eighteen.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Bella Swan (Twilight): She moves to Forks, Washington, a real rainy town in the Pacific Northwest, which now sells Twilight tourism.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Elizabeth Bennet: Jane Austen first called the book First Impressions, and Elizabeth is twenty and quick to judge Darcy.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Jay Gatsby: Fitzgerald's narrator learns he was born James Gatz, and his reinvention is about the American dream.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Frodo leaving the Shire: He sets out from the Shire after inheriting the Ring from Bilbo, who passed it on at his farewell.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Bilbo at his farewell party: His eleventy-first birthday party opens The Fellowship of the Ring, and hobbits only come of age at 33.
Characters' ages in their famous stories.Methuselah at his death: The oldest person in the Bible, he was Noah's grandfather, and his name has become a byword for great age.

Spaces on these game boards.Tic-tac-toe: The board gives rise to a famous fact: with perfect play, the game always ends in a draw.
Spaces on these game boards.Mancala (Kalah): Mancala-style games are among the oldest known board games, with versions played across Africa and Asia for thousands of years.
Spaces on these game boards.Backgammon: Its ancestors go back around 5,000 years, and its 24 points have been laid out by many cultures in a similar way.
Spaces on these game boards.Connect Four: It has been solved by computer: the first player can always win with perfect play.
Spaces on these game boards.Chessboard: The number of possible chess games is vastly bigger than the number of atoms in the universe.
Spaces on these game boards.Sudoku grid: A valid puzzle needs at least 17 given numbers, and the game was invented by an American, Howard Garns.
Spaces on these game boards.Battleship grid: It began as a pencil and paper game before Milton Bradley made it a plastic one in 1967.
Spaces on these game boards.Chinese checkers: It is not Chinese, and was developed from the German game Halma in the 1890s.
Spaces on these game boards.Scrabble board: Alfred Butts invented it as Criss-Crosswords, and it was renamed Scrabble before it took off.
Spaces on these game boards.Go board: Played for over 2,500 years, it has more possible positions than atoms, until AlphaGo beat a top player in 2016.

When these psychology terms were coined.Psychoanalysis: Freud first used the term in 1896, and it grew from the 'talking cure' he developed after working with Breuer's patient.
When these psychology terms were coined.Schizophrenia: Eugen Bleuler coined it from Greek for 'split mind', and it does not mean multiple personalities.
When these psychology terms were coined.Autism: Bleuler first used it to describe withdrawal in schizophrenia; the modern sense arrived with Kanner and Asperger in the 1940s.
When these psychology terms were coined.Stress (Selye's sense): Hans Selye borrowed the word from physics in 1936 to describe the body's response to demands.
When these psychology terms were coined.Gaslight (the film): The 1944 film starring Ingrid Bergman, based on a 1938 play, gave rise to the term for psychological manipulation.
When these psychology terms were coined.Cognitive dissonance: Leon Festinger developed it after studying a doomsday cult in When Prophecy Fails.
When these psychology terms were coined.Midlife crisis: Elliott Jaques coined the term in a 1965 paper.
When these psychology terms were coined.Stockholm syndrome: It was named after a 1973 Stockholm bank robbery in which hostages defended their captors.
When these psychology terms were coined.PTSD (official diagnosis): It entered the DSM-III in 1980, largely due to Vietnam veterans' struggles.
When these psychology terms were coined.Dunning-Kruger effect: Psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger found that weak performers overestimate their skill, inspired by a bank robber who trusted lemon juice.

When these car makers were founded.Cadillac: Named after the founder of Detroit, Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac, it won fame early for interchangeable parts.
When these car makers were founded.Rolls-Royce: Charles Rolls and Henry Royce partnered after meeting in 1904, and its Spirit of Ecstasy mascot dates to 1911.
When these car makers were founded.Bugatti: Ettore Bugatti founded it in Molsheim, Alsace, making artful racing cars, and VW revived the brand later.
When these car makers were founded.Chevrolet: Co-founded by Swiss race driver Louis Chevrolet, who left within a few years, it joined General Motors in 1918.
When these car makers were founded.BMW: It first built aircraft engines, and its blue-and-white roundel is often said to evoke a spinning propeller.
When these car makers were founded.Porsche: Ferdinand Porsche founded his design firm in 1931, and had designed the VW Beetle; its first own car came in 1948.
When these car makers were founded.Toyota Motor Corporation: It began as a loom maker, Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, and changed the spelling to Toyota.
Soichiro Honda began with motorbikes, and Honda is the world's largest motorcycle maker.
When these car makers were founded.Lamborghini: Tractor maker Ferruccio Lamborghini reportedly started it after a spat with Ferrari over a clutch.
When these car makers were founded.Tesla: Named for Nikola Tesla, it hired Elon Musk as an early investor and he became CEO in 2008.

When these dictionaries were first publi.Cawdrey's Table Alphabeticall: This early English wordlist covered only about 2,500 "hard words", and it is considered the first monolingual English dictionary.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Vocabolario della Crusca: Its name means "bran", since the Italian academy behind it meant to sift the good language from the chaff.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Académie française dictionary: The Académie compiled it to fix French usage, and it still publishes rulings that purists debate.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Johnson's Dictionary: Samuel Johnson worked on it for about nine years, with help from a few assistants, and defined lexicographer as a "harmless drudge".
When these dictionaries were first publi.Webster's American Dictionary: Noah Webster's work helped create American spelling, such as color and center instead of colour and centre.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Roget's Thesaurus: Doctor Peter Mark Roget published it after a lifetime of keeping lists of words, and it grouped words by idea instead of by letter.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Duden: Konrad Duden's spelling guide became the standard for German orthography, and the word Duden is now used as a generic term for dictionaries in Germany.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Oxford English Dictionary: The first fascicle appeared in 1884 and the final volume of the first edition came out in 1928, roughly 44 years later, with millions of reader-submitted quotations.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Urban Dictionary: A student wrote it as a joke, and now it's the site people check for the latest slang.
When these dictionaries were first publi.Wiktionary: This online dictionary run by Wikimedia defines words from many languages, in many languages.

Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Pea: Small, soft hail like this rarely causes damage, though hail forms by freezing in layers like an onion.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Marble: Marble-sized hail can dent cars if it falls hard enough, and it's still below the severe threshold.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Quarter: Weather forecasters in the US call a storm severe once its hail reaches an inch, the size of a quarter.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Ping-pong ball: About the size of a ping-pong ball, hail like this can break windows and strip crops.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Hen egg: Hail of this size can damage roofs, and it takes a strong updraft to hold it aloft.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Tennis ball: Updrafts of over 100 mph can hold up tennis-ball-sized hail, which falls at speeds of about 70 mph.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Teacup: Teacup-sized hailstones can cause serious injuries and wreck roofs and cars.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Softball: Stones of softball size can crash through roofs and cause serious injuries.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Grapefruit: Grapefruit-sized hail is very rare, and it needs a supercell thunderstorm.
Hailstones by the names forecasters give.Record (Vivian, S. Dakota): The record stone fell in Vivian, South Dakota, in 2010, and weighed nearly two pounds.

Famous sculptures, by date.Discobolus (Myron's original): Myron's lost bronze of the discus thrower survives only in Roman marble copies, and it's the classic image of the athlete.
Famous sculptures, by date.Venus de Milo: The Venus de Milo was found on the Greek island of Milos in 1820, and her missing arms have fueled endless speculation.
Famous sculptures, by date.Michelangelo's David: Michelangelo carved David from a block of marble that other artists had abandoned, and he finished it when he was 29.
Famous sculptures, by date.Ecstasy of Saint Teresa: Bernini's sculpture in Rome's Santa Maria della Vittoria shows the saint in rapture, a masterpiece of Baroque drama.
Famous sculptures, by date.Statue of Liberty: A gift from France designed by Bartholdi, with an iron frame by Gustave Eiffel, and its full name is Liberty Enlightening the World.
Famous sculptures, by date.The Little Mermaid: Edvard Eriksen's bronze in Copenhagen was commissioned by the brewer Carl Jacobsen, who was captivated by a ballet, and it has been beheaded twice.
Famous sculptures, by date.Christ the Redeemer: This Art Deco Rio de Janeiro statue is 30 meters tall and was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Famous sculptures, by date.Mount Rushmore (completed): Gutzon Borglum and his crew blasted and carved four presidents' faces in the Black Hills, and it took 14 years.
Famous sculptures, by date.Angel of the North: Antony Gormley's steel figure in Gateshead has a wingspan of 54 meters, and its wings are tilted slightly forward.
Famous sculptures, by date.Cloud Gate (the Bean): Anish Kapoor's mirrored steel sculpture in Chicago is made of 168 plates welded together, with no visible seams.

Odd units of time.Planck time: It is roughly the time light needs to cross the Planck length; below that, known physics breaks down.
Odd units of time.Shake: Nuclear physicists coined it, from two shakes of a lamb's tail, and it was used during the Manhattan Project.
Odd units of time.Moment (medieval): Medieval scholars like Bede divided the hour into 40 moments.
Odd units of time.Microcentury: One millionth of a century; computer scientist Tom Duff observed that a 50-minute lecture is about one.
Odd units of time.Sennight: Archaic English for a week, from seven nights, and a cousin of fortnight.
Odd units of time.Fortnight: From Old English for fourteen nights, still in everyday use in Britain and Australia.
Odd units of time.Olympiad: The ancient Greeks counted years in four-year periods between Games, beginning with 776 BC.
Odd units of time.Lustrum: A Roman five-year period that ended with a purification ceremony after the census.
Odd units of time.Jubilee: In the Bible, every 50th year debts were to be forgiven and land returned to its owners.
Odd units of time.Kalpa (Hindu cosmology): A day of the god Brahma in Hindu cosmology is about 4.32 billion years, strikingly near Earth's age of 4.54 billion.

British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.George I: He was a German-speaking Elector of Hanover who spoke little English, and he became king at age 54.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.George II: The last British monarch to lead troops into battle, at Dettingen in 1743.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.George III: His 60-year reign saw the loss of the American colonies, and he suffered bouts of illness that led to a regency.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.George IV: As Prince Regent he lavishly rebuilt the Brighton Pavilion and began turning Buckingham House into a palace.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.William IV: Known as the 'sailor king' for his Navy service, he signed the Great Reform Act of 1832.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.Victoria: Women couldn't inherit Hanover, so her uncle took that crown, ending the link with Britain after 123 years.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.Edward VII: Nicknamed 'Bertie', he waited almost sixty years as Prince of Wales before inheriting the throne.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.George V: Anti-German feeling in the First World War led him in 1917 to rename the royal house from Saxe-Coburg-Gotha to Windsor.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.Edward VIII: He gave up the throne after under a year, to marry Wallis Simpson, a twice-divorced American.
British monarchs from Hanover to Windsor.George VI: A stammer plagued him, and he became king unexpectedly after his brother's abdication; his story inspired The King's Speech.

When these famous firsts happened.First circumnavigation: Magellan's expedition began the circumnavigation, but he died in the Philippines, so Juan Sebastian Elcano completed the voyage.
When these famous firsts happened.First manned balloon flight: The Montgolfier brothers' hot-air balloon carried a sheep, a duck and a rooster in 1783, before the first humans flew.
When these famous firsts happened.First ascent of Mont Blanc: Jacques Balmat and Michel Paccard reached the summit of Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, in 1786.
When these famous firsts happened.First modern Olympics: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens, and a Greek shepherd named Spyridon Louis won the marathon.
When these famous firsts happened.Wright brothers' first flight: The Wright brothers' first flight at Kitty Hawk lasted 12 seconds, and covered about 37 meters.
When these famous firsts happened.Amundsen at the South Pole: Roald Amundsen's Norwegian team reached the South Pole about a month before Scott's British party, using sled dogs to get there.
When these famous firsts happened.Alcock and Brown fly Atlantic: John Alcock and Arthur Brown flew a modified Vickers Vimy bomber nonstop across the Atlantic, from Newfoundland to Ireland.
When these famous firsts happened.Everest summited: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first confirmed to reach the top of Everest, in 1953, during a British expedition.
When these famous firsts happened.Gagarin orbits Earth: Yuri Gagarin's flight lasted 108 minutes, and he made one orbit of Earth, becoming the first human in space.
When these famous firsts happened.First person on the Moon: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on July 20, 1969, and around 600 million people watched on TV.

French inventions and discoveries.Hot-air balloon: The Montgolfier brothers' first passengers were a sheep, a duck and a rooster. Humans flew a few weeks later.
French inventions and discoveries.Metric system: The metre was first defined as one ten-millionth of the distance from the pole to the equator along the Paris meridian.
French inventions and discoveries.Jacquard loom: It used punched cards to weave patterns, which later inspired early computers.
French inventions and discoveries.Stethoscope (Laennec): René Laennec invented it to avoid pressing his ear against a woman's chest. His first version was a roll of paper.
French inventions and discoveries.Braille: Louis Braille developed his system at age 15. He had been blinded in a childhood accident.
French inventions and discoveries.First photograph (Niépce): The picture, from a window at Le Gras, needed an exposure of about eight hours.
French inventions and discoveries.Pasteurization: Pasteur developed it to stop wine spoiling, and only later applied it to milk.
French inventions and discoveries.Lumière cinématographe: The brothers' first public screening was in Paris in December 1895.
French inventions and discoveries.Aqua-Lung: Jacques Cousteau and Émile Gagnan's invention put diving within reach of ordinary people.
French inventions and discoveries.Bikini: Louis Réard named it after Bikini Atoll, where nuclear tests had just been held.

When these canals opened.Canal du Midi: Pierre-Paul Riquet's waterway links the Atlantic to the Mediterranean across southern France. It is a UNESCO site, and plane trees line its banks.
When these canals opened.Bridgewater Canal: Built to carry coal to Manchester, this is often called Britain's first true industrial canal. It slashed the price of coal in the city.
When these canals opened.Erie Canal: Linking the Hudson River to Lake Erie, it turned New York City into the leading US port. It was called "Clinton's Ditch" by sceptics.
When these canals opened.Rideau Canal: Built after the War of 1812 as a safe route for supplies, it runs from Ottawa to Kingston. In winter its frozen length becomes a huge skating rink.
When these canals opened.Suez Canal: Ferdinand de Lesseps's canal links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea. It saves ships a trip around Africa and carries roughly 12% of world trade.
When these canals opened.Manchester Ship Canal: This canal turned Manchester into an inland seaport, about 60 km from the sea. It was the longest river navigation canal in the world when it opened.
When these canals opened.Panama Canal: Ships climb about 26 metres on locks to Gatun Lake and back down. It cut the voyage between the Atlantic and Pacific by thousands of kilometres.
When these canals opened.White Sea-Baltic Canal: Dug in about 20 months in the early Soviet era, largely by forced Gulag labour. It was too shallow for many ships and tragically costly in lives.
When these canals opened.St. Lawrence Seaway: It lets ocean ships travel from the Atlantic deep into the Great Lakes, up to Duluth. Locks lift them about 180 metres along the way.
When these canals opened.Main-Danube Canal: This canal completed a waterway linking the North Sea to the Black Sea. It climbs more than 400 metres across the European watershed.

Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Lifts the boulder: Theseus lifted a heavy rock to find his father's sword and sandals. He then set off for Athens along the dangerous coastal road.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Periphetes the club-man: This club-wielding brigand attacked travellers on the road to Athens. Theseus killed him, and kept the club as his weapon.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Sinis the pine-bender: Sinis bent pine trees down to tie victims and fling them. Theseus defeated him in the same way.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.The Crommyonian Sow: A giant sow terrorised the village of Crommyon, and Theseus killed her. Some tales say she was named Phaia.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Sciron at the cliffs: Sciron made travellers wash his feet, then kicked them off a cliff to a huge turtle. Theseus threw him off.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Cercyon the wrestler: Cercyon challenged travellers to wrestle and killed those he beat. Theseus beat him and is credited with early wrestling rules.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Procrustes and his bed: Procrustes stretched or chopped his guests to fit his bed. "Procrustean" now means forcing things to fit a rigid standard.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Slays the Minotaur: Theseus entered the Labyrinth on Crete and killed the bull-headed monster. He found his way out by Ariadne's thread.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Leaves Ariadne on Naxos: After helping him, Ariadne was left sleeping on the island of Naxos. In some versions the god Dionysus found and married her.
Exploits of Theseus, in story order.Aegeus leaps to his death: Theseus forgot to change his black sail to white as promised. His father threw himself into the sea, now called the Aegean.

First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Dungeons and Dragons: Co-created by Gary Gygax and Dave Arneson, it grew out of the wargame Chainmail.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Traveller: Marc Miller's science-fiction RPG is notorious for allowing characters to die during character creation.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Call of Cthulhu: Based on H.P. Lovecraft, it has players lose Sanity points when they meet cosmic horrors.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Warhammer Fantasy Battle: Games Workshop's fantasy battle game ran for decades before being replaced by Age of Sigmar in 2015.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Paranoia: A darkly comic RPG where players serve a mad computer in a dystopia; every character starts with six clones.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.GURPS: Steve Jackson's 'Generic Universal RolePlaying System' lets you run any setting with the same rules.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Warhammer 40,000: Set in a grim future, its tagline says there is only war.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Shadowrun: It blends cyberpunk, magic and elves in the 2050s, with hackers known as deckers.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Vampire: The Masquerade: White Wolf's game of 'personal horror' launched the wider World of Darkness series.
First editions of these tabletop RPGs an.Pathfinder: Paizo built it from D&D 3.5 rules after the original publisher moved to a new edition.

When these writing tools were invented.Papyrus: Made from a plant of the Nile, it is where our word 'paper' comes from.
When these writing tools were invented.Parchment: Made from animal skin, its name is linked to the city of Pergamum.
When these writing tools were invented.Paper: Credited to Cai Lun; it reached the Islamic world after the Battle of Talas in 751, tradition says.
When these writing tools were invented.Graphite pencil: The 'lead' is actually graphite mixed with clay, a misnomer from Roman 'plumbum'.
When these writing tools were invented.Rubber eraser: Joseph Priestley noted its rubbing ability in 1770, which is why the material was called rubber.
When these writing tools were invented.Typewriter (Sholes): Mark Twain is said to have been one of the first authors to submit a typed manuscript.
When these writing tools were invented.Fountain pen (Waterman): Waterman's feed system finally let ink flow steadily, avoiding blots.
When these writing tools were invented.Ballpoint pen (Bíró): Hungarian László Bíró devised it, and in Argentina such pens are called 'birome'.
When these writing tools were invented.Highlighter: The Hi-Liter, from Carter's Ink in 1963, started as a marking pen for ledgers.
When these writing tools were invented.Post-it Note: Spencer Silver accidentally invented a weak glue at 3M, and Art Fry later used it for bookmarks.

How many of each car model were made.McLaren F1: Only 106 were built, including prototypes and racers; its central driver's seat and 240 mph top speed stood as a record for years.
How many of each car model were made.Bugatti Veyron: Making 1,001 horsepower, it was engineering so costly that Volkswagen reportedly lost money on every one it sold.
How many of each car model were made.Ferrari F40: Launched in 1987, it was the last Ferrari approved by Enzo Ferrari himself, and the first production Ferrari to pass 200 mph.
How many of each car model were made.Lamborghini Countach: Its name is a Piedmontese exclamation of astonishment, reportedly blurted by a worker who first saw the prototype.
How many of each car model were made.DeLorean DMC-12: Its brushed stainless-steel body was built in Northern Ireland, and it became a legend after time-travelling in Back to the Future.
How many of each car model were made.Citroën 2CV: Designed so a farmer could drive across a ploughed field with a basket of eggs unbroken, it stayed in production from 1948 to 1990.
How many of each car model were made.Classic Mini: Alec Issigonis's 1959 design turned the engine sideways to fit in a tiny body; it won the Monte Carlo Rally three times in the 1960s.
How many of each car model were made.Ford Model T: Its moving assembly line in 1913 cut build time from over 12 hours to about 90 minutes, making cars affordable for ordinary families.
How many of each car model were made.Volkswagen Beetle: Designed under Ferdinand Porsche's direction, it overtook the Model T as the most-produced car in 1972.
How many of each car model were made.Toyota Corolla: The best-selling car nameplate in history, it has been on sale since 1966 and passed 50 million sold in 2021.

Europe's great windstorms, in order.Great Storm (Defoe's): Defoe's account describes thousands of chimneys down, and it destroyed the Eddystone lighthouse with its builder inside.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Great Storm (UK and France): BBC forecaster Michael Fish said there would be no hurricane, then it flattened some 15 million trees.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Burns' Day storm (Daria): It killed nearly 100 people across Europe, and struck on the birthday of the poet Robert Burns.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Lothar: It struck on Boxing Day with gusts over 200 km/h, and damaged forests and the gardens of Versailles.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Gudrun: Sweden's worst storm in decades felled about a year's worth of timber in a single night.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Kyrill: It brought chaos to Germany, including closing Berlin's main railway station, and killed dozens.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Klaus: It devastated the pine forests of Les Landes in southwest France and flooded Spanish ports.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Xynthia: A surge flooded France's Atlantic coast, and the aftermath led to new coastal planning laws.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Eunice: It produced a gust of 122 mph on the Isle of Wight, England's record wind speed.
Europe's great windstorms, in order.Ciarán: It battered the Channel coasts, with gusts over 200 km/h in Brittany.

When these revolutions broke out.Glorious Revolution: In 1688 William of Orange landed in England and James II fled almost without a fight, which is why it is called bloodless. It cemented Parliament's power.
When these revolutions broke out.American Revolution: Fighting began at Lexington and Concord in 1775, but independence was only declared a year later. The war lasted until 1783, with French help proving decisive.
When these revolutions broke out.French Revolution: It began with the storming of the Bastille in July 1789. It toppled a monarchy that had lasted centuries, and later gave the world the metric system.
When these revolutions broke out.Haitian Revolution: Enslaved people in Saint-Domingue rose up and created the first Black-led republic in 1804. Toussaint Louverture became its best-known leader.
When these revolutions broke out.Springtime of the Peoples: Also called the Revolutions of 1848, this wave of uprisings swept across Europe in months, from Paris to Vienna and Budapest, and mostly failed in the short term.
When these revolutions broke out.Mexican Revolution: It started in 1910 against the long rule of Porfirio Díaz and ran for about a decade. Leaders such as Pancho Villa and Emiliano Zapata became legends.
When these revolutions broke out.Russian Revolution: Two upheavals in 1917 ended the tsars and brought the Bolsheviks to power. The October one is called that because Russia still used the older Julian calendar.
When these revolutions broke out.Cuban Revolution: Fidel Castro and Che Guevara began as a small guerrilla band in the Sierra Maestra mountains and overthrew Batista, taking Havana on New Year's Day 1959.
When these revolutions broke out.Iranian Revolution: It overthrew the Shah and replaced Iran's monarchy with an Islamic republic led by Ayatollah Khomeini, who returned from exile in Paris in early 1979.
When these revolutions broke out.Velvet Revolution: Czechoslovakia's communist government fell in 1989 after weeks of peaceful protest, with no real bloodshed. Playwright Václav Havel became president soon after.

Rolling sushi, step by step.Rinse the rice: Short-grain Japanese rice is washed several times until the water runs clear. This removes surface starch and keeps the cooked grains from clumping.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Cook the rice: Sushi rice is cooked until sticky but still holds its grain shape. Traditionally it was made with a heavy lid and without lifting it.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Season with rice vinegar: Vinegar, sugar and salt are folded into the warm rice. The word sushi actually refers to the vinegared rice, not the raw fish.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Fan it to cool: Chefs fan the rice while mixing so that it cools fast and becomes glossy. This is why many sushi cooks work with a flat wooden tub called a hangiri.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Lay nori on a bamboo mat: Nori is dried, pressed seaweed. The rolling mat, called a makisu, is made from thin bamboo slats tied together with string.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Spread rice over the nori: Hands are dipped in water so the rice does not stick. The rice goes on in a thin, even layer, leaving a strip of nori bare at the far edge.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Line up the fillings: Classic fillings include cucumber, tuna or avocado. The California roll, with the rice on the outside, was invented in North America.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Roll it up tight: The mat helps squeeze the roll into a firm, even cylinder. A tight roll keeps the pieces from falling apart when sliced.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Slice with a wet knife: Wiping a very sharp knife with a damp cloth stops the rice from sticking. A clean, single sawing cut gives neat pieces.
Rolling sushi, step by step.Dip in soy sauce: Dip the fish side and not the rice, which soaks up too much. Wasabi is often fake, made from horseradish and colouring, outside Japan.

Ages and eras of history, in order.Stone Age: The oldest known stone tools, found at Lomekwi in Kenya, are about 3.3 million years old, older than the Homo genus itself.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Bronze Age: Bronze is copper alloyed with tin, and since tin was rare, it had to travel long distances, creating early trade networks.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Iron Age: Iron became widespread around 1200 BC, partly because the Bronze Age collapse disrupted tin supplies and made iron useful.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Classical antiquity: Classical antiquity covers Greece and Rome; Homer is traditionally dated near 800 BC and the first Olympics to 776 BC.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Middle Ages: The term Middle Ages was coined by later scholars who saw it as a gap between classical Rome and their own era.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Renaissance: Renaissance means rebirth, and the movement began in Florence, where wealthy families like the Medici funded artists.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Age of Enlightenment: The Enlightenment championed reason, with thinkers such as Newton, Voltaire and Kant, and it influenced the American and French revolutions.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Industrial Revolution: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain with textile mills and steam power, and it eventually reshaped how most people lived and worked.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Atomic Age: The first atomic bomb test, Trinity, took place in the New Mexico desert in July 1945, weeks before Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
Ages and eras of history, in order.Space Age: The Space Age began with Sputnik 1, a beeping metal ball launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957, which alarmed the West.

Comedians, by birth year.Charlie Chaplin: His Tramp character, with the bowler hat and cane, made him one of the first global film stars, and he also composed music for his films.
Comedians, by birth year.Groucho Marx: With his greasepaint mustache and quick one-liners, he hosted the hit quiz show You Bet Your Life for years.
Comedians, by birth year.Buster Keaton: Nicknamed 'The Great Stone Face' for never smiling on screen, he did his own dangerous stunts in silent films.
Comedians, by birth year.Bob Hope: He entertained American troops overseas for decades with USO shows and hosted the Academy Awards nearly twenty times.
Comedians, by birth year.Lucille Ball: Her sitcom I Love Lucy was the first to be filmed with several cameras before a live audience, a method still used.
Comedians, by birth year.Robin Williams: Famous for lightning improvisation, he also earned an Oscar for a dramatic supporting role in Good Will Hunting.
Comedians, by birth year.Eddie Murphy: He joined Saturday Night Live at 19 and became a major star in the early 1980s, soon after leaving for films.
Comedians, by birth year.Jim Carrey: Known for rubber-faced comedy in Ace Ventura and The Mask, he also gave memorable dramatic performances in The Truman Show.
Comedians, by birth year.Tina Fey: She became the first female head writer of Saturday Night Live and created the sitcom 30 Rock, based partly on that work.
Comedians, by birth year.Kevin Hart: Starting in stand-up, he sold out stadiums and was among the highest-earning comedians of the 2010s.
